## Antibody Backbone to Sequence Generation

Antibody Backbone to Sequence Generation

### Public interface guidance

Design amino-acid sequences for antibody-chain backbone structures using PiFold/ProDesign inverse folding. Supply a ZIP of backbone PDB files and select heavy- or light-chain mode. Each backbone must use chain A. The designed sequences can support subsequent structure and antibody-property evaluation.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_name` | string | Required | envelope | Tool identifier: Antibody_Backbone_to_Sequence_Generation. It selects the tool, not the experiment label. The connector generates experiment_name when omitted; preserve an exact label only when supplied by the user. |
| `dataPath` | string | Required | file | ZIP containing non-empty PDB backbone files directly at the archive root. Each structure must contain chain A. PDB files in nested directories are not accepted. |
| `mode` | string | Required | value | Antibody chain type: H for a heavy-chain backbone or L for a light-chain backbone. Both modes require the backbone to be identified as chain A in the PDB. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product result guidance: Designed full-chain amino-acid sequences with calculated sequence properties. Heavy/light compatibility and antigen binding require separate evaluation.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `Antibody_Backbone_to_Sequence_Generation`.

### Inputs

Fields below belong in `experiment_data`. The connector generates `experiment_name` unless the user supplies one.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dataPath` | string | yes | file | ZIP containing PDB backbone files; each must contain chain A, which the helper parses for both H/L modes. |
| `mode` | string | yes | value | `"H"` or `"L"` |

Input kinds: `value` is inline data; `file` requires a platform file reference;
`file_or_value` supports either documented mode; `artifact` is an authorized upstream result reference.
Only local files require a new upload. Never infer input mode from a field name.

## Backbone Generation

Backbone Generation

### Public interface guidance

Generate antibody heavy- and light-chain backbone structures in one run using Protein Frame Flow. Supply the required H/L mode label and a sampling count. Both chain collections are generated for either mode value, with sampling distributed across configured chain lengths. The two backbone collections are returned separately for subsequent sequence design.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_name` | string | Required | envelope | Tool identifier: Backbone_Generation. It selects the tool, not the experiment label. The connector generates experiment_name when omitted; preserve an exact label only when supplied by the user. |
| `mode` | string | Required | value | Required chain-mode label: H for heavy chain or L for light chain. Both heavy- and light-chain backbone collections are generated for either value; this label does not restrict the output to one chain type. |
| `n_samples` | integer | Required | value | Requested backbone sampling count. Enter a whole number of at least 7. Samples are distributed over configured chain lengths, so the final count may differ. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product result guidance: Separate PDB archives for heavy-chain (H) and light-chain (L) backbones. Both archives are produced in the same run. Sampling is distributed over chain lengths, so the delivered count can differ from the requested sampling count.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `Backbone_Generation`.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `n_samples` | integer | yes | value | Number of structures |
| `mode` | string | yes | value | `"H"` or `"L"` |

Input kinds: `value` is inline data; `file` requires a platform file reference;

## CDR Generator

CDR Generator

### Public interface guidance

Generate antibody heavy-chain sequence variants by replacing one CDR with EvoDiff-generated sequence. The selected numbering scheme locates HCDR1, HCDR2 or HCDR3 in the full heavy-chain sequence. The surrounding sequence is retained as context.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | Required | value | Supported antibody chain mode: H. Supply a full heavy-chain sequence and select HCDR1, HCDR2 or HCDR3. Light-chain CDR generation is not supported. |
| `sequence` | string | Required | value | Full heavy-chain amino-acid sequence using the 20 standard residues. The selected CDR is replaced while the surrounding sequence is retained. |
| `scheme` | string | Required | value | Antibody numbering scheme used to locate the CDR: imgt, kabat or chothia. |
| `cdr_reg` | string | Required | value | Heavy-chain region to regenerate: HCDR1, HCDR2 or HCDR3. |
| `n_samples` | integer | Required | value | Number of full-length sequence variants to sample. Enter a positive integer. |
| `file_format` | string | Required | value | Output format: csv only. The CSV includes generated heavy-chain sequence variants and calculated sequence properties. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product result guidance: A CSV of full-length heavy-chain sequence variants with the selected CDR replaced and calculated sequence properties. Generation is not conditioned on an antigen.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `CDR_Generator`.

### Inputs

Fields below belong in `experiment_data`. The connector generates `experiment_name` unless the user supplies one.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence` | string | yes | value | Input antibody sequence (NOT `seq`) |
| `file_format` | string | yes | value | CSV is the supported output format. |
| `n_samples` | integer | yes | value | Number of sequences |
| `scheme` | string | yes | value | Operator confirmed chothia, not chotia. |
| `cdr_reg` | string | yes | value | `"HCDR1"`, `"HCDR2"`, `"HCDR3"` |
| `mode` | string | yes | value | Operator confirmed 2026-09-12: H only. Never submit L. |
| `property_name` | string | no / mode-dependent | value |  |

Input kinds: `value` is inline data; `file` requires a platform file reference;
`file_or_value` supports either documented mode; `artifact` is an authorized upstream result reference.
Only local files require a new upload. Never infer input mode from a field name.

## Random Antibody Generation

Random Antibody Generation

### Public interface guidance

Generate antibody heavy- and light-chain sequence libraries with IgLM and calculate sequence properties. Both chain types are generated in one run and returned as separate CSV files. The chains are sampled independently, so the results are libraries for subsequent pairing and evaluation rather than confirmed antibody pairs.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_name` | string | Required | envelope | Tool identifier: Random_Antibody_Generation. It selects the tool, not the experiment label. The connector generates experiment_name when omitted; preserve an exact label only when supplied by the user. |
| `n_samples` | integer | Required | value | Requested sampling count. Enter a whole number of at least 16. Heavy chains are sampled in groups of 8 and light chains in groups of 16, with each count rounded down independently. |
| `file_format` | string | Required | value | Output format. Use csv. Heavy- and light-chain sequences and their calculated properties are returned in separate CSV files. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product-interface limits (not overrides of connector validation): Use an integer sampling count of at least 16. Heavy-chain counts are rounded down to groups of 8 and light-chain counts to groups of 16.

Integration limitation: The product guidance mentions 16 samples, but this connector currently requires an integer greater than 16 (minimum 17). Use the installed connector constraint; this documentation does not change or bypass it.

Product result guidance: Separate heavy- and light-chain CSV files containing sequences and calculated properties. The collections do not represent confirmed heavy/light pairs or antigen-specific antibodies.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `Random_Antibody_Generation`.

### Inputs

Fields below belong in `experiment_data`. The connector generates `experiment_name` unless the user supplies one.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `n_samples` | integer | yes | value | Hard constraint: integer greater than 16 (minimum 17). The UI/sample value is 20 and is the recommended normal minimum. |
| `file_format` | string | yes | value | `"csv"` or `"fasta"`; user-facing alias `format`. These and `n_samples` are the only user input fields. |

Input kinds: `value` is inline data; `file` requires a platform file reference;
`file_or_value` supports either documented mode; `artifact` is an authorized upstream result reference.
Only local files require a new upload. Never infer input mode from a field name.
